_note: Tooling reference (parity B3). What each free publisher prints, transcribed by BenchMate with URL and access date. Values are as printed; a value is confirmed only when two independent publishers print it. Nothing is typed in from memory. Text statements in the tooling guide carry the same source keys (app/tooling.js).

OSG.title: Tap drill size and pitch diameter limit chart, vol. 3, 2024
OSG.note: Tap maker. H1 to H6 through 1 in (each 0.0005 in wide, max = basic + n x 0.0005); over 1 in to 1-1/2 in H4 = basic + 0.0010 to + 0.0020; D3 to D9 as inch offsets over basic; recommended H and D numbers per size and class.

USCTI.publisher: US Cutting Tool Institute (information from GWS Tool Group)
USCTI.title: Tapping tips: How H-limits relate to class of fit (part 1) and Finding the perfect tap
USCTI.note: Trade association page, written by a tap maker group. H and L numbers 0.0005 in each; D and DU numbers 0.013 mm each; minimum of H (and maximum of L) from the tap standards (ASME B94.9). Its M6 x 1 example uses a basic pitch diameter of 5.530 mm in the sums and 5.350 mm in the text (ISO 724 gives 5.350); the sums are kept as printed, the slip is noted.

MSC.title: Taps buying guide; Thread forming taps buying guide
MSC.note: Distributor. H numbers 0.0005 in each through 1 in, e.g. H3 = basic + 0.0010 to + 0.0015; choose the largest H number that still gives the class of fit. Forming taps: drill = D - (0.0068 x %)/TPI; a metric line printed with an extra 0.0068 factor (see form_tap); and the shortcut D - P/2.

CTS.title: Manufacturing tips: H limits and class of fit
CTS.note: Distributor. H steps of 0.0005 in above the minimum (go gauge); the 40 % rule: put the tap about 40 % of the part tolerance above the minimum.

NAT.title: TRU-FLO thread forming taps, engineering data (spec sheet 19000)
NAT.note: Tap maker. Hole = D - 0.0068 x % / TPI; metric hole = D - % x P / 147.06; 55 % for the largest and 75 % for the smallest hole as a guide.

BESLY.publisher: Besly Products Corp. (D. Gajdosik), in Cutting Tool Engineering
BESLY.title: Threads will roll, Cutting Tool Engineering, 1 Aug 1995
BESLY.note: Tap maker's engineer. Hole = tap OD - 0.0068 x % / TPI; 65 to 75 % is enough for general work; forming not recommended above 75 %. Old (1995) but matches the current makers.

FMC.title: TechTips: tapping formulas
FMC.note: Tool seller. Forming tap constants 0.68 (as % / 100) and 147.06 (metric). Already used by the Tap drill size tool.

EE.title: Theoretical tapping hole size, cold form threads
EE.note: Engineering reference site. Forming tap hole with 0.0068. Already used by the Tap drill size tool.

BALZERS.title: Cutting tools coating overview HQ189EN (2509)
BALZERS.note: Coating maker. Max service temperature per coating: BALINIT A (TiN) 600, B (TiCN) 400, LATUMA and BALIQ ALTINOS (AlTiN based) 1000, OPTURA (TiAlN based) 1100, ALCRONA EVO and BALIQ ALCRONOS (AlCrN based) 1100, BALDIA COMPOSITE (CVD diamond) 600 deg C. Brand coatings: one value per chemistry family taken from the base coating named.

HARTNER.title: Coatings (HARTNER_Beschichtungen_EN)
HARTNER.note: Drill and tool maker. Max application temperature (printed as < value): TiN 600, TiAlN 800, AlTiN 900, TiCN 450, DLC 500, CVD diamond 600, ZrN 700 deg C.

GWS.title: Tool coatings
GWS.note: Tool maker. TiN 500 deg C; AlTiN 800 deg C, printed as an oxidation temperature. No temperature for TiCN, TiAlN or DLC.

BRYCOAT.title: PVD coating properties
BRYCOAT.note: Coating service. Max service temperature: TiN 600, TiCN 400, TiAlN 800, AlTiN 800, CrN 700, ZrN 600 deg C.

IJS.publisher: Jozef Stefan Institute, Department F3 (thin films)
IJS.title: Coating types
IJS.note: Research institute. Max temperature: TiN 500, CrN 750, TiAlN 900, AlTiN (nano-layer AlTiN/TiN) 1100 deg C.

PRODINC.title: Selecting the right end mill for your machining set up, 21 Apr 2026
PRODINC.note: Distributor. Flutes by material, end shapes, roughers, variable pitch and helix, coatings by work material.

BROTHER.title: What is an end mill? (Speedio navi article a0046), 11 Jun 2024
BROTHER.note: Machine tool maker. Flute count trade-offs, square, ball and radius ends, roughing end mills.

REGAL.title: Which drill point angle should I be using?, 30 Oct 2024
REGAL.note: Drill maker. 118 deg general purpose; 135 deg for harder materials such as stainless; point styles.

TRAVERS.title: How to choose the right drill (2025); Tapping right (2021)
TRAVERS.note: Distributor. Drill types, 118 and 135 deg split points, over 140 deg for very hard alloys, spot drill angle at least the drill's; tap types and chamfers (taper about 9, plug about 4, bottoming 1 to 2 threads).

GAMMONS.title: Reaming FAQ
GAMMONS.note: Reamer maker. Left-hand spiral for through holes, right-hand spiral for blind holes, straight flute general; stock about 3 % of diameter, typically 0.004 to 0.012 in; about two thirds of drilling speed.

CUTWEL.title: Types of reamers
CUTWEL.note: Distributor. Straight flute for blind and through holes, left-hand spiral pushes chips ahead (through holes), right-hand spiral pulls them back (blind holes); machine, hand, adjustable, taper pin reamers.

STARRETT.title: Sawing starts with the material, 4 May 2023
STARRETT.note: Saw blade maker. No fewer than 3 and no more than about 10 to 14 teeth in the material (rule of thumb for soft materials); larger work, coarser pitch.

RMT.title: Do I have the right TPI and tooth pitch for my cut?
RMT.note: Saw machine dealer. Minimum 3 teeth in contact, preferably 6 to 12.

RAPID.title: How to remove broken taps (2022, updated 2026)
RAPID.note: Machining service. Extractors, punch and pliers, chisel, EDM, redrilling or grinding, chemical dissolving, welding a nut; prevention tips.

AIMS_BT.title: How to remove a broken tap: 6 methods, tools and prevention, 2026-09-29
AIMS_BT.note: Tool supplier. Extractor (clean break, M6 or larger), EDM, carbide end mill, thread repair insert, alum on aluminium parts, welding a rod or nut to the stub, prevention.

MFGSHOP_BT.title: Shane, How to remove a broken thread tap: step-by-step guide, 2025-05-29
MFGSHOP_BT.note: Extractor, hammer and punch with pliers, EDM, carbide or cobalt drill, thread insert, welding, prevention. No chemical methods.

HARVEY_TM.title: Understanding CNC threads, taps, and thread mills (In the Loupe article hosted by Tormach, no date)
HARVEY_TM.note: Tool maker. Single form, tri-form and multi-form cutters; climb milling direction for right and left hand internal threads; several radial passes; three axes at once; chip evacuation.

MSC_TM.title: Thread milling informational guide (no date)
MSC_TM.note: Distributor; same publisher as MSC. One tool for many diameters of one pitch, right and left hand, internal and external; compared with tapping.

IMD_TM.title: Thread milling: climb vs conventional milling for CNC, 2026-05-08
IMD_TM.note: Right-hand thread with a clockwise spindle: feeding up (+Z) is climb milling; left-hand: feeding down. Does not separate internal from external, so used for internal threads only, where Harvey says the same.

PROTOOL_TM.title: Thread milling: the complete guide for precision engineers, 2026-06-22
PROTOOL_TM.note: Tool supplier. Full profile, partial profile and single profile cutters; compared with tapping; climb milling up the wall of an internal thread; several orbits in tough material.

REGAL_TG.title: Expert's guide to the 4 basic features of tap geometry (no author or date shown)
REGAL_TG.note: Tap maker; same publisher as REGAL. Positive and negative hook by chip type, relief, substrate, surface treatments. No angles in degrees.

GSR_RAKE.title: Angle of rake: the angle of rake of the tap (Threading tools guide blog), 2020-02-03
GSR_RAKE.note: Tap maker. Rake matched to the material group; colour rings, with no common system among makers. No angles in degrees.

AIMS_CF.title: Cutting fluids & cutting oils: types, selection & applications guide, 2026-09-29
AIMS_CF.note: Tool supplier; same publisher as AIMS_BT. Fluids for hand and machine tapping, and by work material.

XO_TAP.publisher: Xometry (K. de Naoum, updated by M. Conniff)
XO_TAP.title: 15 different types of thread taps, 2024-01-30, updated 2026-03-12
XO_TAP.note: Manufacturing network. Pipe taps, extension taps, interrupted thread taps, combined drill and tap.

CCB_TAP.title: 10 types of taps for threads and how to choose, last modified 2024-04-11
CCB_TAP.note: CNC reference site. Pipe taps straight and tapered, extension taps, interrupted thread taps.

PT_TH.title: Lathe tool holders carbide: what to choose, 2026-06-14
PT_TH.note: Tool supplier. Shank size, overhang, clamping kinds named, interrupted cuts, what to check before ordering.

MMC_TH.title: Tool holder selection for external turning (course page)
MMC_TH.note: Maker. Clamping methods P, S, C, D, M and E and where each is used; square inserts. Its tables of holders and lead angles are images and were not read.

OMT_TH.title: CNC turning tool holder types: the ultimate selection guide, 2025-12-30, modified 2026-11-02
OMT_TH.note: Seller. Clamping kinds, shank, overhang, hand, positive inserts. Its list of style letters and angles contradicts itself and is not used.

VIK_TS.title: BE ME 6th sem: concept of rake and clearance angles and tool signature
VIK_TS.note: University course notes. The seven elements of the signature in order, angles in degrees and nose radius in mm, with the example 0-7-6-8-15-16-0.8.

TB_TS.title: ASA tool signature: objective questions with answers
TB_TS.note: Exam practice site. The same order of the seven elements; angles in degrees; the nose radius is given in inches in one answer and in mm in another.

RS.title: How to use thread-forming taps, 2026
RS.note: Distributor. Forming taps suit soft materials such as aluminium and soft steel; no chips and no flutes; formed threads generally stronger than cut.

_tap_limits_note: USCTI prints the D step as 0.013 mm; stored here converted to inch (0.013 / 25.4 = 0.000512) so it can be compared with OSG's inch offsets. MSC and OSG are independent (distributor and maker); USCTI is GWS Tool Group's text and CTS is a distributor.

MSC.metric_div: MSC prints (0.0068 x % x P) / 147.06: the 0.0068 is applied twice, which gives a hole almost at the major diameter. Read it as % x P / 147.06.

_form_tap_note: 147.06 = 1 / 0.0068, so the inch and metric forms are the same rule. MSC's shortcut D - P/2 equals the rule at 73.5 % thread. Balax (forming tap maker) prints hole sizes 0 to 0.0016 in larger than the rule for miniature sizes (see docs/sources.md, Tap drills).
